newsitem.title: UK: Colossal Zambian cobalt slag project progresses.
newsitem.headline: Colossal Zambian cobalt slag project progresses.

text.p: Colossal Resources Corp said on Monday they were pleased with the development of the Nkana slag dump located 160 miles north of Lusaka, Zambia.
At a presentation in London Colassal's President and Chief Executive Officer Dil Gujral said he believed the project was advancing smoothly and was experiencing few technical problems.
Colossal said Nkana is considered to be the largest surface cobalt deposit in the world which contains 56,000 tonnes of cobalt and 80,000 tonnes of copper.
The estimated value of the cobalt content is approximately $2.5 billion based on $25/lb metallic cobalt.
An induction furnace for setting and granulating the cobalt rich alloy will be implemented in November.

A 10-tonne electric furnace will be installed in December when slag processing should increase to the planned first year level of about 300 tonnes per day, yielding near 40 tonnes of contained cobalt per month.

Referring to cobalt's supply/demand outlook over the next few years Gujal said he expected a shortfall of around 6,000 tonnes to develop, against a backdrop of increasing demand and despite future new production projects.
"There is likely to be no new production for around four years," he said.
By 2,000 Colossal estimated an additional demand of 10,000 tonnes from the battery industry.
In 1994 Colossal signed a joint partnership agreement to acquire 60 percent of Qasim Mining Enterprises Limited (QMEL).

Through QMEL, Colossal entered into a contractual agreement with Zambian Consolidated Copper Mining Ltd (ZCCM), a large producer of copper and cobalt, to recover around 8.6 million tonnes of cobalt metal from the Nkana slag dump. In the European free market Russian material has eased slightly to settle at around $21.75/$22.50, still well above 23-month lows of $18/$19 seen in August. High grade metal was indicated at $22.75/$23.50.
